title: Anticipatory flushing and fairness probes
body:
Overview:

This is a working log for a small series of probes that explore an "anticipatory flush" heuristic plus lightweight fairness guards in the continuous-batching scheduler. The goal was to reduce p99 tail latency for small interactive requests without materially harming throughput or causing starvation for background/low-priority traffic.

Motivation / context:
- Several customer workloads show a bimodal request size distribution: 70% short prompts (<32 tokens) and 30% long generation jobs (>512 tokens).
- Our existing time-based flush (fixed timeout ~10ms) keeps throughput high for long jobs but creates p99 spikes for short requests during microbursts where batch fill stalls.
- Prior experiments (see linked artifacts) covered dynamic timeouts and prioritized batching; this set focuses on preemptive/anticipatory flush triggers that are cheap and local to a queue slice.

Hypotheses tested:
1) Adding an anticipatory flush that triggers when estimated remaining headroom is small (based on recent arrival rate and slot occupancy) will reduce p99 for short prompts by allowing earlier dispatch of near-full-but-waiting batches.
2) A minimal fairness guard (age-based priority increment + soft demotion for long-running batch owners) prevents starvation of lower-priority lanes with negligible throughput loss.
3) There is a sweet spot where p99 improves substantially while batch efficiency (tokens/second/GPU) drops by <6%.

Experiment setup:
- Cluster: 4x A100-80GB nodes (same as canary cluster).
- Runtime: serving-runtime branch 'anticipatory-probes' with NVTX markers added around queueing and flush decisions.
- Metrics collected: queue_wait_ms, batch_size_mean, batch_fill_pct, batch_flush_count, p50/p95/p99_latency_ms, gpu_util_pct, tokens_per_sec_per_gpu, kv_cache_hit_rate, preemptions_count.
- Workloads: synthetic replay + live-shadow of two customers:
  - Interactive (short): Poisson arrivals, mean inter-arrival 4ms, prompt length 16 tokens, target tail-sensitive.
  - Background (long): bursts of 1k long jobs with avg length 800 tokens, throughput-focused.
- Duration: 2-hour runs per configuration, repeated 3x.

Key heuristics implemented:
- Anticipatory flush: if (now - batch_first_enqueue_time) >= base_timeout * alpha OR estimated_time_to_fill > flush_window then flush. Estimated_time_to_fill uses EWMA arrival rate per lane and remaining slots. Alpha tuned in sweeps (0.6/0.8/1.0).
- Soft fairness demotion: lanes accrue "age_credits"; if lane starves > demotion_threshold (ms) it gets a temporary priority bump for next N batches. Conversely, lanes that monopolize GPU cycles for >long_owner_window get demoted one priority level for a grace period.
- Admission control: cap on concurrent inflight long batches per GPU to reduce head-of-line blocking.

Representative run results (median of 3 runs):
- Baseline (fixed timeout 10ms, no anticipatory flush):
  - p50: 34ms, p95: 212ms, p99: 870ms
  - mean batch_size (short lane): 5.8 requests, batch_fill_pct: 42%
  - gpu_util_pct: 78%, tokens_per_sec_per_gpu: 1.1M

- Anticipatory flush (alpha=0.8, demotion_threshold=120ms):
  - p50: 36ms, p95: 126ms, p99: 480ms  (p99 improved ~45%)
  - mean batch_size (short lane): 6.3, batch_fill_pct: 48%
  - gpu_util_pct: 74%, tokens_per_sec_per_gpu: 1.04M (drop ~5.5%)
  - preemptions_count: +2% (more small batch preempts), kv_cache_hit_rate: unchanged (+/-1%)

- Aggressive anticipatory (alpha=0.6):
  - p50: 38ms, p95: 102ms, p99: 420ms
  - mean batch_size: 5.1, batch_fill_pct: 39%
  - gpu_util_pct: 69%, tokens_per_sec_per_gpu: 0.96M (drop ~12.7%)
  - Observed more batch churn and slight increase in gpu context switches (measured via nvidia-smi sampling).

- Anticipatory + stronger fairness (age bump + tighter demotion window):
  - p99 (short lane): 460ms, background throughput drop <2% vs anticipatory baseline
  - Observed helpful reduction in observed starved low-priority queues (queue_wait_ms 95th decreased by ~40% for low-priority).

Profiling observations (NVTX / traces):
- The largest contributor to p99 in baseline runs was queueing variance: some short requests queued behind a long batch that was just about to dispatch; the long batch then hit a kernel path that increased kernel latency (attention patterns), amplifying tail.
- With anticipatory flush, NVTX showed earlier dispatch of near-full short batches; the kernel scheduling variance was reduced because smaller batches increase opportunity to interleave short jobs across kernels.
- However, increased batch flush frequency raised CPU overhead in the coalescer thread (~+14% sys time for the coalescer) and increased small memcpy ops on the host.

Edge cases and failure modes observed:
- Under extreme long-job heavy bursts, anticipatory flush without admission control caused throughput collapse: too many small batches saturated H2D transfer lanes. Adding the inflight-long-batches cap stabilized the cluster.
- For models with heavy KV cache dependency (decoder-only long-context), anticipatory flushing sometimes reduced effective cache reuse, increasing per-token compute time by 3-6% in worst cases. This was mitigated by a cache-awareness rule that suppresses anticipatory flush when recent kv_cache_hit_rate drops below a threshold.

Operational notes / instrumentation gaps:
- We needed higher-resolution sampling for per-batch GPU context switch counts; current sampling (1s) is too coarse. Action: add 100ms smoothed counters to the trace exporter.
- Need separate counters for small-batch memcpy volume vs normal batches to quantify host-to-device bandwidth impact.

Conclusions so far:
- Anticipatory flush reduces short-request p99 materially with small throughput cost when tuned carefully (alpha ~0.8).
- Fairness guards (age bump + light demotion) are effective at preventing starvation and keep background throughput stable.
- Production rollouts must include: inflight-long-batches cap, kv-cache-aware suppression, and telemetry to track memcpy pressure.

Recommended next steps / rollout plan:
1) Implement conservative alpha=0.8 global flag behind feature gate; A/B test on 5% of traffic for 2 weeks, monitor p99, tokens/sec, memcpy_bytes metrics.
2) Add the long-batch inflight cap to the admission controller and enable by default in the flag.
3) Add a KV-cache suppression rule: if kv_cache_hit_rate < 70% over sliding 30s, disable anticipatory on that lane for 10s.
4) Expand tracing: 100ms GPU context switch sampling + per-batch memcpy counters.
5) If A/B signals are positive, schedule gradual ramp with canary in 3 regions.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Quantify dollar cost impact for hosted customers (need cost model per small-batch increase).
- Evaluate interaction with quantized kernels (does the memory churn differ?).
- Explore hybrid heuristics: combine anticipatory flush with brief randomized jitter to avoid synchronized flush storms.
- In longer term, consider ML-based arrival-rate predictor to replace EWMA.

Immediate action items (owners):
- Miguel: add per-batch memcpy counters to trace exporter (SRV-5128).
- Priya: kick off 5% A/B flag rollout and dashboard (dashboard template in Confluence).
- Ethan: implement kv-cache suppression and long-batch cap in admission control branch.
- Asha: consolidate logs and schedule a cross-team sync (eng-sre + infer-research) after first 5% run.

Notes to self / rough command snippets used during profiling:
- Start NVTX traces: RUNTIME_TRACE=1 task=queueing ./deploy-canary.sh --nodes 4
- Quick sampler (host): watch -n0.2 "nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory,utilization.gpu --format=csv"
- Trace export: ./trace-exporter --group serving-runtime --tags anticipatory-probe --sample-rate 100ms

Appendix: example lightweight pseudo-code for anticipatory flush (simplified):

  enqueue(req, lane):
    slice = lane.active_slice
    slice.append(req)
    slice.last_enqueue = now
    slice.fill_count += 1

  coalescer_tick(slice):
    arrive_rate = slice.arrival_ewma
    slots_left = slice.max_size - slice.fill_count
    est_time_to_fill_ms = (slots_left / max(1e-6, arrive_rate))
    if (now - slice.first_enqueue >= base_timeout * alpha) or (est_time_to_fill_ms > flush_window_ms):
      flush(slice)

(See linked PR for full implementation details.)

-- end of notes --
